title: Spotify Running — product film

location.extent: Representative frame; complete local animation linked

slide_intent: Explain personalization through a physical activity because an abstract promise becomes easier to understand when viewers see music respond to their pace.
strategic_value: Spotify can differentiate a listening service through tempo detection and running-specific music choices shown within an everyday activity.
demonstration: The 51-second film intercuts runners, a phone detecting tempo, short yellow-magenta title cards and messages including Music that reacts to you.
practical_value: Study how live action, interface evidence and short benefit statements work together in a product story.

content_islands.name: Running footage
content_islands.spec: Outdoor runners and close views of moving feet establish the activity and pace.

content_islands.name: Interface demonstration
content_islands.spec: A centered phone shows tempo detection with a prominent numeric readout.

content_islands.name: Message cards
content_islands.spec: Short large statements alternate with footage and flat high-contrast color fields.

reference_purposes.Expression: The 51-second film intercuts runners, a phone detecting tempo, short yellow-magenta title cards and messages including Music that reacts to you.
reference_purposes.Application: The source shows this identity in a running-product film.
reference_purposes.Intent: The film explicitly promises Music that reacts to you, alongside tempo detection and running footage; it supplies a reason for matching music to running pace.
